rv.q: This dame makes a hell of a Queen.
Happily, Zeldin 's script is also very funny: understated but wincingly convincing in the manner of the best TV mockumentaries.
The problem really is Morgan's blandly amusing but desperately trivial script.
Kristin Scott Thomas succeeds on the throne with her own special brand of twinkling irony and glacial dignity.

cn.t: Critics praise this top-notch revival, with Kristin Scott Thomas proving a fascinating and credible successor to Helen Mirren, bringing twinkling irony and glacial dignity to Peter Morgan's cunning play about the Queen's private audiences with her prime ministers.
